candidates.evaluate_with: Add it as a pinned dependency (registry version or git rev) of a scratch workspace crate with the exact feature set proposed for the slim profile, then run this audit on that Cargo.lock. Also audit what a feature named runtime-core actually excludes (a feature name is not proof), its background and blocking worker threads, and its u64 atomics (the BE targets have no atomic64): contract E03 section 4.
candidates.name: asupersync

candidates.evaluate_with: Pin it the same way and read the std/alloc columns at the exact revision: its transitive no_std and alloc choices must be validated, not assumed (no_std is not no allocation).
candidates.name: franken_kernel

candidates.evaluate_with: FrankenLibC reuse is admitted function by function after target review (contract E03 section 4): pin the revision, audit its closure with this tool, and review each function against the target ABI. The Rust `libc` crate is not a candidate for this row: it is an FFI binding table, reported on its own row below.
candidates.name: libc candidates

candidates.evaluate_with: The Rust `libc` crate declares C types and functions for FFI. It is not a libc and nothing to admit: its presence on a big-endian target graph means code there can call C functions through it, so review which functions are called against the target ABI (contract E03 section 4). A presence on the host reference platform only is the build machine's, not the firmware's.
candidates.name: libc crate (Rust FFI binding table)
candidates.status: present only on the reference platform (host); absent from every big-endian target graph

candidates.evaluate_with: No codec crate is named anywhere in this repository. Name candidates first (S02 codec profile qualification), then audit each pinned closure, including its floating-point use on the soft-float MIPS target.
candidates.name: codecs
